rows.reasoning: Hilton says "politicians shouldn't draw their own maps" and praises taking map-drawing "out of the hands of the politicians" through California's citizens independent districting process. That puts him on the independent-commission side, against legislature-drawn maps. But he never says whether he wants a commission with "no elected officials involved at any level" or one "with equal representation from both major parties", so the evidence does not choose between those two rungs.

quotes.text: We all agree, I think, that politicians shouldn't draw their own maps. I mean, that's obviously wrong and corrupt.

Texas didn't change its constitution to take the power to draw the maps out of the hands of the politicians, put it in the hands of the people, which we did here with the two ballot initiatives in 2008 and 2010 um to set up the citizens independent districting uh process.
I think prop 50 was I mean, I totally disagree to try to stop it. It's unconstitutional and so on, and made those arguments in court.
